title: Checkpoints Make Cells Wait, Then Commit

scenes.tts: Irradiate a budding yeast cell that lacks a gene called Rad nine. It does not pause. It keeps dividing for several generations, and it dies. Hold the same cell back with a drug for a few hours, and it repairs the damage. So what was the gene for?
scenes.caption: Irradiate a budding yeast cell that lacks a gene called RAD9. It does not pause. It keeps dividing for several generations, and it dies. Hold the same cell back with a drug for a few hours, and it repairs the damage. So what was the gene for?
scenes.visual: An irradiated cell with broken DNA divides again and again and dies; the same cell held by a drug repairs its DNA; a question mark over the gene.
scenes.narration: Irradiate a budding yeast cell that lacks a gene called RAD9. It does not pause. It keeps dividing for several generations, and it dies. Hold the same cell back with a drug for a few hours, and it repairs the damage. So what was the gene for?

scenes.tts: Rad nine was not a repair gene. It was a gene for waiting. Hartwell and Weinert named such a control a checkpoint. A checkpoint makes one cell cycle event wait for another. Remove it, and the cell still divides, but on time instead of on completion.

scenes.visual: Event A fills a bar; a red gate holds event B until the bar is full; then the gate is removed and B goes at a fixed time with the bar part full.
scenes.narration: RAD9 was not a repair gene. It was a gene for waiting. Hartwell and Weinert named such a control a checkpoint. A checkpoint makes one cell-cycle event wait for another. Remove it, and the cell still divides, but on time instead of on completion.

scenes.tts: Before anaphase, every pair of sister chromatids must attach to opposite poles, at a site called the kinetochore. In a P t K one cell, one chromosome was attached to only one pole. Rieder's group destroyed its unattached kinetochore with a laser, and anaphase followed about twenty minutes later. That chromosome never reached the middle. So the wait signal comes from an unattached kinetochore.

scenes.visual: A spindle with attached chromosomes and one with an unattached kinetochore; a laser removes it; a timer reads 20 plus or minus 2.5 minutes; the other sisters part.

scenes.tts: Unattached kinetochores promote assembly of the mitotic checkpoint complex, made of Mad two, C D C twenty, Bub R one and Bub three. C D C twenty is the activator that the A P C slash C ligase needs to pick its mitotic targets. Bub R one carries sequences that mimic a target's binding sequence, and they sit in the binding sites of C D C twenty. It is a key broken off in the lock.
scenes.caption: Unattached kinetochores promote assembly of the mitotic checkpoint complex, made of Mad2, Cdc20, BubR1 and Bub3. Cdc20 is the activator that the APC/C ligase needs to pick its mitotic targets. BubR1 carries sequences that mimic a target's binding sequence, and they sit in the binding sites of Cdc20. It is a key broken off in the lock.
scenes.visual: Four chips gather into a red MCC box; Cdc20 joins the APC/C blob as a cup with a slot; the BubR1 tab fits into the slot like a broken key.

scenes.tts: When the last kinetochore attaches, the checkpoint complex releases its grip. A P C slash C with C D C twenty ubiquitinates securin and cyclin B, and the proteasome destroys them. Securin had held separase, a protease, inactive. Freed, separase cuts S C C one, the cohesin that holds sister chromatids together. Anaphase begins.

scenes.visual: The key lifts out of the slot; ubiquitin badges mark securin and cyclin B and both vanish into the proteasome; separase wakes and cuts the cohesin link; sisters part.

scenes.tts: Here is a made up time course for securin in HeLa cells. After metaphase, it falls from one hundred percent to fifty in ten minutes, so its half life is ten minutes. Add a spindle poison at ten minutes, and the fall stops near fifty. A phosphate can be removed in seconds, but a destroyed protein must be made again. So a checkpoint makes the cell wait, and destruction makes the move one way.
